rgesn.intro: These questions complete the automatic measurements. Answer for your service.
rgesn.1.1: Have you weighed the service’s usefulness against its impacts?
rgesn.1.2: Have you described the people aimed at and their real needs?
rgesn.1.3: Is an ecodesign lead named for this service?
rgesn.1.4: Do you regularly review whether your approach is followed?
rgesn.1.5: Have you set targets to reduce impact?
rgesn.1.6: Is data collection limited to what the service needs?
rgesn.1.7: Is encryption proportionate to the service’s needs?
rgesn.1.8: Have you published part of the service as open code?
rgesn.1.9: Does the service rely on open, interoperable standards?
rgesn.1.10: Do exchanges with hardware go through open APIs?
rgesn.2.1: Have you listed the devices that can use the service?
rgesn.2.2: Does the service still work on older devices?
rgesn.2.3: Does the service stay usable on a slow connection?
rgesn.2.4: Does the service work on older systems and browsers?
rgesn.2.5: Does the layout adapt to phone, tablet, and computer?
rgesn.2.6: Do the design and the code aim to reduce impacts?
rgesn.2.7: Have you planned maintenance and the end of the service?
rgesn.2.8: Do your suppliers commit to reducing their impacts?
rgesn.2.9: Have you weighed the impact of ready-made interface components?
rgesn.2.10: Have you weighed the impact of third-party services before choosing them?
rgesn.3.1: Is the architecture designed to limit its own impacts?
rgesn.3.2: Do resources adapt to the service’s real use?
rgesn.3.3: Can the service follow protocol changes?
rgesn.3.4: Are fixes provided for the whole planned lifetime?
rgesn.3.5: Can a fix be installed without a product upgrade?
rgesn.3.6: Do updates send only what changed?
rgesn.3.7: Are test environments used only when needed?
rgesn.4.1: Do videos, sounds, and animations stay stopped at the start?
rgesn.4.2: Does the service avoid endless scrolling of content?
rgesn.4.3: Is each main journey short and direct?
rgesn.4.4: Can the person choose to turn on a third-party service?
rgesn.4.5: Do you mostly use components the platform already provides?
rgesn.4.6: Do videos, sounds, and animations carry useful information?
rgesn.4.7: Do you choose the lightest medium that meets the need?
rgesn.4.8: Is the number of downloaded fonts limited?
rgesn.4.9: Does typing avoid a server request on every keystroke?
rgesn.4.10: Is the expected format shown before the form is sent?
rgesn.4.11: Are the weight and the format of files announced before sending?
rgesn.4.12: Do you warn when a feature has an important impact?
rgesn.4.13: Are notifications rare and can they be turned off?
rgesn.4.14: Does the interface avoid tricks that push more use?
rgesn.4.15: Can the person follow and reduce the impact of their use?
rgesn.5.1: Does each image use a format suited to its content?
rgesn.5.2: Is each image’s compression suited to its use?
rgesn.5.3: Does each video have a definition suited to its display?
rgesn.5.5: Do videos offer listening without the picture?
rgesn.5.6: Is the audio compression suited to listening?
rgesn.5.7: Does each document use a format suited to its use?
rgesn.5.8: Are outdated contents archived or deleted?
rgesn.6.1: Are a maximum weight and a request count set per screen?
rgesn.6.2: Are the contents you control cached on the visitor’s side?
rgesn.6.3: Are the texts you control compressed when sent?
rgesn.6.4: Do images have dimensions close to the display?
rgesn.6.5: Do you avoid loading unused resources?
rgesn.6.6: Are the device sensors turned on only when needed?
rgesn.6.7: Do your static files leave from a single domain name?
rgesn.7.1: Is there a server cache for the most requested data?
rgesn.7.2: Do data have a retention period, then a deletion?
rgesn.7.3: Is a treatment in progress shown, to avoid a double send?
rgesn.7.4: If a blockchain is used, is its consensus sober?
rgesn.8.1: Does the host publish an approach to reduce impact?
rgesn.8.2: Does the host have a durable policy for its equipment?
rgesn.8.3: Is the hosting PUE published and low?
rgesn.8.4: Is the hosting water use tracked and limited?
rgesn.8.5: Is the hosting electricity documented and mostly renewable?
rgesn.8.6: Is the hosting located where electricity is low-carbon?
rgesn.8.7: Is server heat recovered or well controlled?
rgesn.8.8: Are rarely read data separated from active data?
rgesn.8.9: Are data copies limited to what is strictly needed?
rgesn.8.10: Do deferred treatments avoid consumption peaks?
rgesn.9.1: Is training a model really necessary for the service?
rgesn.9.2: Is the learning phase proportionate to real use?
rgesn.9.3: Have you limited the amount of training needed?
rgesn.9.4: Are the training data reduced to what is strictly needed?
rgesn.9.5: Are retraining runs spaced according to real need?
rgesn.9.7: Is inference set to limit the resources used?

mq.m.127: The formula, and why it is reproducible
mq.m.128: The overall grade is not an opinion: it is a strict weighted average of the 8 graded areas. Indicators outside the grade never distort it.
mq.m.130: Score equals the sum of area grades times their weight, divided by the sum of active weights
mq.m.139: . A site without mail is therefore not penalised on its grade.

mq.m.143: Our probes run in ephemeral containers: a new audit under the same network conditions produces the same raw data.

mq.m.149: Why are availability and reputation outside the grade?
mq.m.152: is a binary connectivity state at one moment, not an intrinsic quality of the site. The
mq.m.154: depends on third-party lists (RBL, spam filters) that move independently of the code. Putting them in the average would add noise: they stay separate advisory indicators (specification v3, §1 and §6).
mq.m.155: How does Audixio handle application firewalls (WAF such as Cloudflare)?
mq.m.156: When a WAF or a waiting page (JS challenge, Turnstile) blocks the passive read, the probe never forces access. The area becomes
mq.m.158: and the formula removes its weight from the denominator: no site is given a 0 for deploying a legitimate protection.

fix.seo.lighthouse.title: Make the site more visible in search
fix.seo.lighthouse.why: A low SEO score makes the site less visible in search.
fix.seo.lighthouse.netlify.1: Give every page a title and a description.
fix.seo.lighthouse.netlify.2: Let search engines read the page, with no noindex rule.
fix.seo.lighthouse.netlify.3: Add the reference address of the page.
fix.seo.lighthouse.netlify.4: Publish again, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.lighthouse.github_pages.1: Give a title and a description in the HTML file.
fix.seo.lighthouse.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not let you set HTTP headers.
fix.seo.lighthouse.github_pages.3: Alternative: fix the text in the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.lighthouse.generic.1: Give a title, a description and a reference address.
fix.seo.lighthouse.generic.2: Remove any rule that hides the page from search engines.
fix.seo.lighthouse.generic.3: Run the audit again once the change is live.
fix.seo.noindex.title: Keep the page in the results
fix.seo.noindex.why: A noindex instruction removes the page from search results.
fix.seo.noindex.netlify.1: Open the HTML file of the page.
fix.seo.noindex.netlify.2: Remove the tag that contains noindex.
fix.seo.noindex.netlify.3: In `_headers`, do not add the line that hides the page.
fix.seo.noindex.netlify.4: Publish again, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.noindex.github_pages.1: Remove the noindex tag from the HTML file of the repository.
fix.seo.noindex.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not let you remove an HTTP header.
fix.seo.noindex.github_pages.3: Alternative: if the header comes from elsewhere, put a service in front of the site.
fix.seo.noindex.generic.1: Remove the noindex tag from the page.
fix.seo.noindex.generic.2: Remove the header that contains noindex.
fix.seo.noindex.generic.3: Run the audit again once the change is live.
fix.seo.robots.title: Let search engines read the site
fix.seo.robots.why: A robots file that is too strict stops search engines from reading the site.
fix.seo.robots.netlify.1: Create `robots.txt` at the root of the published site.
fix.seo.robots.netlify.2: Do not forbid the whole site if you want to be found.
fix.seo.robots.netlify.3: Add the address of the sitemap.
fix.seo.robots.netlify.4: Publish again, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.robots.github_pages.1: Put `robots.txt` at the root of the domain, not in a subfolder.
fix.seo.robots.github_pages.2: Limit: a site in a subpath does not publish the root file.
fix.seo.robots.github_pages.3: Alternative: host the site at the root, or remove the ban.
fix.seo.robots.generic.1: Publish `robots.txt` at the root of the domain.
fix.seo.robots.generic.2: Allow reading of the pages you want to show.
fix.seo.robots.generic.3: Run the audit again once the change is live.
fix.seo.sitemap.title: Publish a readable sitemap
fix.seo.sitemap.why: A sitemap helps search engines find every page.
fix.seo.sitemap.netlify.1: Create `sitemap.xml` at the root of the published site.
fix.seo.sitemap.netlify.2: List the final address of each page, the one that answers.
fix.seo.sitemap.netlify.4: Publish again, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.sitemap.github_pages.1: Upload the sitemap at the root of the domain, with the final addresses.
fix.seo.sitemap.github_pages.2: Limit: a site in a subpath does not publish the root sitemap.
fix.seo.sitemap.github_pages.3: Alternative: host the site at the root, or list the sitemap in the root robots file.
fix.seo.sitemap.generic.1: Publish a sitemap at the root, with the final addresses.
fix.seo.sitemap.generic.2: Every address must answer without moving to another page.
fix.seo.sitemap.generic.3: Run the audit again once the change is live.
fix.seo.title.title: Write a clear title
fix.seo.title.why: The title is the first line read in the search result.
fix.seo.title.netlify.1: Open the HTML file of the page.
fix.seo.title.netlify.2: Set a single title, about 15 to 60 characters long.
fix.seo.title.netlify.3: Describe this page, not only the site name.
fix.seo.title.netlify.4: Publish again, then run the audit again.
fix.seo.title.github_pages.1: Write a single title in the HTML file of the repository.
fix.seo.title.github_pages.2: Limit: none on the title, the HTML file is edited in the repository.
fix.seo.title.github_pages.3: Alternative: keep the title in the page, not in an HTTP header.
fix.seo.title.generic.1: Set a single title in the head of the page.
fix.seo.title.generic.2: Aim for 15 to 60 characters that describe this page.
fix.seo.title.generic.3: Run the audit again once the change is live.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.title: Show a consent banner
fix.vie_privee.cmp.why: Without a banner, the visitor cannot choose what is stored.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.netlify.1: Add a banner before the trackers load.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.netlify.2: The banner must offer accept and refuse in the same place.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.netlify.3: Netlify does not add this banner on its own.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.netlify.4: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.github_pages.1: Add the banner in the repository template.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not provide a choice banner.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.github_pages.3: Alternative: a script in the repository can show accept and refuse.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.generic.1: Show a banner from the first page.
fix.vie_privee.cmp.generic.2: The visitor must be able to accept or refuse without searching.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.title: Publish a privacy page
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.why: The visitor must be able to read what the site does with their data.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.netlify.2: Describe the data read, its purpose and how long it is kept.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.netlify.3: Add a “Privacy” link in the footer of the home page.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.netlify.4: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.github_pa: Add the page and the link in the repository.
Limit: GitHub Pages does not write this page for you.
Alternative: an HTML page in the repository, linked from the home page.
Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.generic.1: Publish a page that explains the data used.
fix.vie_privee.confidentialite.generic.2: Link to it from the home page with the word “Privacy”.
fix.vie_privee.elements.title: State the publisher, the host and a contact
fix.vie_privee.elements.why: Without these three details, the visitor does not know whom to write to.
fix.vie_privee.elements.netlify.2: Add the publisher, the host and a contact address.
fix.vie_privee.elements.netlify.3: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.elements.github_pages.1: Complete the legal notice page in the repository.
fix.vie_privee.elements.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not know your publisher.
fix.vie_privee.elements.github_pages.3: Alternative: write these three items in the repository page.
fix.vie_privee.elements.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.elements.generic.1: Name the publisher of the site.
fix.vie_privee.elements.generic.2: Name the host and give an email or a phone number.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.title: Publish a readable legal notice
fix.vie_privee.mentions.why: The visitor must be able to know who runs the site.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.netlify.2: Write the publisher, the host and a way to get in touch.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.netlify.3: Add a “Legal notice” link in the footer of the home page.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.netlify.4: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.github_pages.1: Add the page and the link in the repository.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not write the legal notice for you.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.github_pages.3: Alternative: an HTML page in the repository, linked from the home page.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.generic.1: Publish a legal notice page, with real text.
fix.vie_privee.mentions.generic.2: Link to it from the home page with the words “Legal notice”.
fix.vie_privee.refus.title: Offer “Reject all” on the first layer
fix.vie_privee.refus.why: Refusing must be as easy as accepting, from the first screen.
fix.vie_privee.refus.netlify.3: Do not hide the refusal on a second screen.
fix.vie_privee.refus.netlify.4: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.refus.github_pages.1: Edit the banner in the repository files.
fix.vie_privee.refus.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages cannot add this button.
fix.vie_privee.refus.github_pages.3: Alternative: write the button in the page, on the first level.
fix.vie_privee.refus.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.refus.generic.1: Show “Refuse all” on the first screen of the banner.
fix.vie_privee.refus.generic.2: A refusal must close the banner without setting anything more.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.title: Host scripts and fonts yourself
fix.vie_privee.tiers.why: A file loaded elsewhere sends the visitor address to that site.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.netlify.1: Download the fonts and scripts you use.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.netlify.2: Put them in the repository, for example under `/fonts` and `/js`.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.netlify.3: Replace the addresses from another site with these paths.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.netlify.4: Publish, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.github_pages.1: Copy the fonts and scripts into the repository.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not bring these files home for you.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.github_pages.3: Alternative: serve them from the same repository as the pages.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.generic.1: Replace each font or script from another site with a local copy.
fix.vie_privee.tiers.generic.2: Check that no outside address remains in the page.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.title: Wait for a choice before trackers
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.why: A tracker contacted too early fires without the visitor deciding.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.netlify.1: Open the code of the home page.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.netlify.2: Remove the analytics and advertising scripts from the initial load.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.netlify.3: Add them only after the visitor clearly agrees.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.netlify.4: Audience measurement can run without consent if it stays strictly limited.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.netlify.5: Publish the site, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.github_pages.1: Remove the third-party scripts from the HTML template of the repository.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.github_pages.2: Limit: GitHub Pages does not block these scripts for you.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.github_pages.3: Alternative: load them only after consent, in your code.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.github_pages.4: Publish the repository, then run the audit again.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.generic.1: Find the scripts that contact another site as soon as the page opens.
fix.vie_privee.traceurs.generic.2: Move them after the consent button.
